reuse.why: The daily rule is written as a special branch inside getNextDate instead of extending the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend or the rschedule conversion that getUpcomingDates and schedule-template also use.

duplication.why: No logic is copied, but the occurrence query is re-issued inside a loop that restates the forward/reverse lookup of the surrounding code.

placement.why: The weekend decision lives in a shared helper in this tree, yet the new rule is placed in one consumer (getNextDate) and reads frequency from dateCond.value rather than the schedule data the other weekend settings come from.

scope.why: Only getNextDate and a focused test change.

maintainability.why: The weekend rule now differs between getNextDate and the other paths (upcoming dates, schedule templates) that still move daily weekend occurrences via getDateWithSkippedWeekend, so a maintainer has to know about the hidden special case.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate handles daily weekend occurrences with its own isWeekend loop rather than through getDateWithSkippedWeekend / recurConfigToRSchedule, the abstractions the other weekend paths share.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic; the problem is a local special case, not a copy.

one_place.where: The rule is applied only in getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts); getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts and schedule-template.ts still call getDateWithSkippedWeekend for daily schedules.
